title: Grammar: Advanced Narrative Devices — Inversion, Discourse Markers, Sentence Variety
grammarTip:
Профессиональный нарративный стиль — три секрета:

① РАЗНООБРАЗИЕ длины предложений:
Короткие = удар, ударение, драма.
Длинные создают плавность, показывают связь между идеями.

② КОНКРЕТНЫЕ детали вместо общих слов:
Вместо "it was cold" → "frost had formed on the windows"
Вместо "she was nervous" → "her hands were shaking"

③ ПОКАЗЫВАЙ, а не рассказывай (Show, don't tell):
❌ "He was very angry." → ✅ "He slammed the door without a word."
❌ "She was happy." → ✅ "She couldn't stop smiling all morning."

grammarTable.example: Slowly, she turned. Outside, the storm was growing. There, on the table, was a letter.

grammarTable.subject: Discourse markers
grammarTable.example: Meanwhile, in another part of the city... / Suddenly, everything changed.

grammarExtra.title: Fronting: Moving Elements to the Beginning

rows.example: "At midnight, the city was finally quiet."
"Carefully, she lifted the photograph from the drawer."
"On the floor, among the scattered papers, she found what she was looking for."
"Never had she felt so alone." "Not once did he mention her name."

rows.form: No sooner + had + subject + pp + than…
rows.example: "No sooner had he arrived than the argument started."
"There, on the step, stood a figure she recognised."

rows.form: Sequence: first, then, next, finally, eventually
rows.example: "Eventually, after hours of silence, he spoke."

rows.form: Time shift: meanwhile, in the meantime, at the same time
rows.example: "Meanwhile, across town, something else was happening."

rows.form: Sudden change: suddenly, all at once, without warning
Contrast: however, but, despite this, even so
rows.example: "She smiled. Despite this, her eyes were cold."
"He ran. He fell. It was over."
"The afternoon light stretched long and golden across the floor, and in it the dust moved slowly, as if the air itself were considering whether to stay."
"She opened the envelope. A single sheet of paper. No date. No signature."
"Her hands were shaking." / "He slammed the door without a word."
"The coffee went cold while she sat staring at the letter." = showing preoccupation.

opts: She had never felt so afraid.
Never she had felt so afraid.
Never had she felt so afraid.
exercises.correct: Never had she felt so afraid.

exercises.text: "She carefully opened the drawer." → ___, she opened the drawer.
exercises.hint: Move the manner adverb to the front

exercises.instruction: Which is an example of "showing" rather than "telling"?
opts: His voice cracked as he tried to speak.
exercises.correct: His voice cracked as he tried to speak.
exercises.hint: Showing = emotion expressed through physical action/detail

exercises.text: "Not once ___ he ___ (look) at her during the whole conversation."
exercises.hint: Not once + did + subject + bare infinitive

exercises.instruction: Which discourse marker signals a sudden change?
Which sentence creates dramatic impact through short sentences?
opts: The room was dark and cold, and she could hear rain falling against the window.
She stood. She stared. She ran.
Walking slowly, she approached the door, uncertain of what she might find inside.
The long corridor stretched out before her, its walls covered in faded photographs.
exercises.correct: She stood. She stared. She ran.
exercises.hint: Short sentences = impact at a climax moment

exercises.text: "___, in another part of the building, someone was listening." (= at the same time)
exercises.hint: Meanwhile = at the same time, in a different location

opts: His coffee was cold on the table.
She was devastated by the news.
exercises.correct: She was devastated by the news.

exercises.text: "He was very angry." → He ___ the door ___ without saying a word.
exercises.hint: Show anger through physical action, not the word "angry"

opts: No sooner she left than he called.
No sooner had she left than he called.
No sooner she had left when he called.
No sooner did she leave than he had called.
exercises.correct: No sooner had she left than he called.
exercises.hint: "No sooner had + subject + pp… than + past simple"

exercises.instruction: What effect does this create? "She waited. And waited. And waited."
exercises.hint: Deliberate repetition = emphasises how long / how much

exercises.text: "___ the table was a small, folded piece of paper." (= There, on the table)

exercises.instruction: Which creates the strongest atmosphere through sentence length?
opts: The fog lay heavy over the river, blurring the lights on the far bank into soft, amber smears.
exercises.correct: The fog lay heavy over the river, blurring the lights on the far bank into soft, amber smears.
exercises.hint: Longer sentences build atmosphere through detail and rhythm

exercises.text: "He sat at the table for a long time. ___, he picked up the phone."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses contrast discourse correctly?
opts: He looked calm. Eventually, he was nervous.
He looked calm. Meanwhile, he was terrified inside.
He looked calm. Despite this, he was terrified inside.
He looked calm. Without warning, he was terrified inside.
exercises.correct: He looked calm. Despite this, he was terrified inside.
exercises.hint: "Despite this" = contrast between outward appearance and inner feeling

exercises.instruction: Transform: "She had never felt this way before." → Dramatic inversion:
opts: Before, she had never felt this way.
Never had she felt this way before.
She never had felt this way before.
Never she had felt this way before.
exercises.correct: Never had she felt this way before.
exercises.hint: Never + had + subject + pp = dramatic inversion

questions.text: "___ had she seen anything so strange in her life." (Dramatic inversion)
questions.hint: Never + had + subject + past participle = dramatic inversion

questions.text: "___, she turned to face him." (Manner adverb fronted for emphasis — slowly)
Which is an example of "showing" rather than "telling"?
opts: She stared at the photo for a long time without speaking.
questions.correct: She stared at the photo for a long time without speaking.
questions.hint: Showing = emotion through action, not the emotion word itself
Not once + did + subject + bare infinitive

questions.text: "___, in a room at the end of the corridor, a light came on." (= at the same time, different location)
"She was angry" is an example of showing, not telling.
Which creates a strong climax through sentence length?
opts: The afternoon was warm and pleasant, and the birds were singing in the trees outside.
He stopped. He looked. He ran.
Walking carefully through the long corridor, she noticed many things she had not seen before.
There were many people waiting in the room when she arrived.
questions.correct: He stopped. He looked. He ran.
questions.hint: Short sentences = maximum impact at dramatic moments

questions.text: "No sooner ___ she ___ (open) the letter than she burst into tears."
"Without warning, the lights went out." What does "without warning" signal?
opts: A time shift to the past

questions.text: "The table, the chairs, the walls — everything was covered in dust." This uses…
questions.hint: Listing items = building emphasis through repetition

questions.text: "___ this, she smiled. Inside, she was breaking." (= contrast marker)
questions.hint: "Despite this" = outward behaviour contrasts with inner feeling

questions.text: Which correctly fronts a place phrase for emphasis?
opts: She found it under the bed.
Under the bed she found it.
Under the bed, she found it.
Found under the bed, she it.
questions.correct: Under the bed, she found it.
questions.hint: Place phrase fronted: "Under the bed, she found it."
